To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the generating functional approach leads to a new diagrammatic expansion for the equal‐time Green functions and that the sum of all terms that correspond to one proper Feynman graph can be expressed in terms of the sum of all graphs that correspond to the original Feynman diagram and a finite number of graphs that have a smaller number of loops than the original diagram.

the equal‐time Green functions in Coulomb gauge can be expressed in terms of the equal‐times vacuum wave functional, that the latter is given in terms (i.e., is generated by) the equal‐time generating functional and that the latter is a functional of the vacuum wave functionals of the free theory.

the generating functional for the equal‐time two‐point correlation function is given in terms the vacuum wave functional and that the sum of all different contributions that correspond in covariant theory to one and the identical proper Feynman graph can be expressed as a sum of two‐point correlation functions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of Dyson‐Schwingerequations for the equal‐time two‐point functions in Coulomb gauge QED.
a systematic approach to the noncovariant perturbation theory of gauge field theories.
the construction of a Dyson‐Schwingerequation‐like formalism for equal‐time correlations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, although the equal‐time theory is nonrenormalizable and nonunitary, the sum over all contributions to a given Feynman diagram is renormalizable and unitary.

the equal‐time Green’s functions of Coulomb gauge QED and QCD are given by a Dyson‐Schwiner equation with the sum of all the different contributions that correspond one to one and the other to the other to the same Feynmann diagram in covariant QED and QED.
the equal‐time Green functions are not well behaved in the Coulomb gauge and, therefore, the Coulomb gauge is not suited for a perturbative approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Dyson‐Schwingerequation for the vacuum wave functional is the starting point for the derivation of the Dyson‐Schringer equations for the correlation functions.
, by using the new diagrammatic rules, one can calculate the equal‐time correlations functions directly from the generating functional.
the Dyson‐Schwingerequations for the equal‐time Green’s functions can be derived from the functional equations for the generating functional of these Green’s functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Dyson‐Schinger equations for the equal‐time Green functions are obtained as a byproduct of the generating functional approach.
the Dyson‐Schwingerequations are not only valid in the time‐ordered formalism but can be extended to equal‐time correlationfunctions as well.

the Dyson‐Schwingerequations for equal‐time Green functions can be formulated for the sum of the different contributions that correspond one and the same proper Feyman diagram, and that the corresponding equations can be solved by iteration.
